content: If you are told that another has spoken ill of you, do not answer him, but laugh, and say: 'The man was ignorant of my other faults, or he would not have mentioned these alone.'
author: Epictetus
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Loneliness is the painful ache of feeling incomplete, while solitude is the rich discovery of your own inner presence. In a world full of constant stimulation and notifications, being alone with your thoughts can feel intimidating.

Epictetus understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Yet silence is the only space where you can hear what your life is actually trying to say to you. When you make peace with quiet, you stop running to distractions to save you from yourself.
reflectionPrompt: What would change in your daily outlook if you truly lived by this perspective?

practicalInsight: Spend fifteen minutes today in complete silence without a screen, podcast, or chore. Just sit and let your mental dust settle.
originalQuote: If any one tells you that another has spoken ill of you, do not make excuses about what you are doing, but answer: 'If he had known my other faults, he would not have mentioned these alone.'
